speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me when the wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions first started and if they appeared together or at different times? Also, have you noticed any joint swelling or redness in other areas of your body?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you notice any circular, expanding rash on your body after the camping trip, or were you bitten by a tick? I also need to know if you have had any recent sexual encounters that might increase the risk of gonococcal infection.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of migratory joint pain, fever, and painless violaceous lesions on an acral distribution after camping in Minnesota is highly suggestive of disseminated gonococcal infection. DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection
